Topics: Reading Information - Integration Of Knowledge & Ideas
SubTopics: Analyze a case in which two or more texts provide conflicting information on the same topic and identify where the texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretation.
Content: Which statement `bbtext(best)` describes a `bbtext(difference)` between the `text(two)` passages?

A.Choice: The passage from “Sally Ride's Legacy Lives On” recounts developments that happened in the `text(1970s)`, while the passage from “To Make It to the Moon ...” focuses on modern space exploration.

B.Choice: The passage from “Sally Ride's Legacy Lives On” discusses only Sally Ride's experiences, while the passage from “To Make It to the Moon ...” includes the perspectives of many women.

C.Choice: The passage from “Sally Ride's Legacy Lives On” expresses opinions about women's rights, while the passage from “To Make It to the Moon ...” remains neutral about women's rights.

D.Choice: The passage from “Sally Ride's Legacy Lives On” is written by an objective author, while the passage from “To Make It to the Moon ...” is written by an author who has an emotional connection to the topic.

SubTopics: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
Content: The author of the passage from “Sally Ride's Legacy Lives On” and the author of the passage from “To Make It to the Moon, Women Have to Escape Earth's Gender Bias” both discuss equality for women in the space program. Write an argument establishing which author provides a more compelling message about the effectiveness of NASA's efforts to increase equality for female astronauts. Be sure to use evidence from `bbtext(both)` passages to develop your argument.
